question.text: The Musket Wars were a series of conflicts fought between the iwi, or tribes, of these Polynesian natives of New Zealand.
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.text: A month later, at this June 1942 battle near an atoll, Americans led by Chester Nimitz won, sinking four Japanese fleet carriers, but losing the speedily-repaired USS Yorktown.
swap.clue: The winning side in this battle lost the (+) Yorktown, whereas the losing side of this battle lost 4 aircraft carriers.

question.text: Guadalcanal was the first major land campaign during a theater of World War II named for this ocean. The Midway Atoll and Pearl Harbor were used by the Navy in this ocean.
question.answerHtml: Pacific Ocean [accept Pacific Theater or Pacific War or Asia–Pacific War]
question.clue: A war named for this body of water included clashes over Tacna and Arica and was partly ended by the Treaty of Ancon (an-KOHN).

swap.leadin: This kingdom's Law of the Splintered Paddle allowed all civilians to travel in peace.
swap.text: Name this kingdom, which was ruled from ʻIolani Palace. Sanford Dole helped overthrow this kingdom's last ruler, Queen Liliʻuokalani [luh-lee-uh-wo-kuh-LAA-nee].
swap.clue: An attempt to replace the Bayonet Constitution led to the overthrow of this kingdom by a group including Sanford Dole.

question.leadin: Identify the following World War II battles of the Pacific Theater.
question.text: The Pacific Theater also included this battle, which was not only the largest naval battle of the war, but in all of history. It included several kamikaze attacks and commenced after the Allies invaded the Phillipines.
question.clue: Admiral Kurita withdrew from this battle which would be the last major action of the Japanese navy until Operation Ten-Go.

swap.text: Frank Bainimarama has ruled this South Pacific country since a 2006 coup. Tension between the native Melanesians and those of Indian descent makes up a significant part of this country's politics.
swap.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

question.text: Lili'uokalani was the last sovereign ruler of this kingdom until it was annexed by the United States in 1898.
question.clue: Its final ruler was forced to sign Lorrin Thurston's Bayonet Constitution, and this kingdom was succeeded by a republic led by Sanford Dole.

swap.leadin: This monarch was the subject of the Morgan and Blount reports.
swap.text: Name this last queen of Hawaii. She was overthrown by the Committee of Safety including Sanford Dole and Lorrin Thurston.
swap.clue: This last monarch and only Queen of the Hawaiian Islands.

question.leadin: The US fought much of World War II in the Philippines.
question.text: Japanese Lieutenant General Homma Masaharu was executed for war crimes as a result of ordering this movement from Mariveles to Camp O'Donnell during which up to ten thousand of seventy thousand POWs succumbed.
question.clue: During World War II, tens of thousands of Filipino and American P.O.W.s were sent on a death march named for this Philippine peninsula. Over ten thousand Filipino P.O.W.s were killed on this death march.

swap.text: The US was brought to the brink of war with Germany by a 1899 civil war in this Pacific island nation. That crisis in this nation was resolved when a typhoon heavily damaged both fleets.
swap.clue: This country's independence was demanded on "Black Saturday" by the Olaf Frderick Nelson-led Mau Movement.

question.leadin: This treaty gave the British dominion over a certain country, with provisions for the continuation of Rangatiratanga, or chieftainship.
question.text: Name this treaty that established a British governor of New Zealand.
question.clue: James Prendergast termed this text a "simple nullity".

swap.leadin: In the 1880s, this island was ruled by the English-Jewish-Tahitian merchant Alexander Salmon, who promoted the production of counterfeit rongorongo scripts.
swap.text: Give the European name for this isolated Pacific island whose population was annihilated in the late 19th century. This island's huge moai statues are sometimes referred to as its namesake heads.
swap.clue: This island's undeciphered rongorongo ("RON-go-RON-go") script has a glyph for the god Makemake ("MAH-kay-MAH-kay").

question.leadin: The expansion of these people were theorized in the "entangled bank" and "express train" models.
question.text: Name these Austronesian people who settled Pacific Islands like Easter Island and Hawaii. These people settled further east, unlike the Melanesians and Micronesians.
question.clue: The range of the non-native sweet potato in places settled by these people supports genetic evidence of contact with Pre-Columbia Americans.

swap.leadin: The women's Mau movement emerged to oppose colonial rule in this country after the Black Saturday massacre.
swap.text: Name this Polynesian country where the Mau movement opposed New Zealand's colonial rule in the late 1920s and early 1930s. This country was colonized after German-backed rebels were defeated in the Siege of Apia.
swap.answerHtml: Independent State of Samoa [accept Western Samoa; do NOT accept or prompt on “American Samoa”]

question.leadin: Signed by President McKinley in 1898, the joint resolution advocated for by this man succeeded where the previous treaty failed due to the Ku'e Petitions.
question.text: The Newlands Resolution, advocated for by this man, saw the transfer of Hawaii to the US as a new territory in 1898. This man served as President of the Republic of Hawaii, and was the cousin of the founder of the Hawaiian Pineapple Company.
question.clue: Lorrin Thurston and John Stevens conspired with this businessman to overthrow Queen Liliuokalani. He was the only president of the Republic of Hawaii.

swap.leadin: Lorrin Thurston and John L. Stephens led the overthrow this monarch, establishing a government under Sanford Dole.
swap.text: Name this monarch who resisted the influence of the Missionary Party in the wake of the Bayonet Constitution being forced on her brother David.
swap.clue: A group of revolutionaries known as a "committee of public safety" and led by Lorrin Thurston rebelled against this leader in order to gain rights for citizens born of American parents.

question.text: The Samoan independence movement was named after this native word, roughly translated as "resolute testimony." An earlier movement named after this word was led by the Pule ("poo-LAY") chief Lauaki Mamoe ("lao-AH-kee muh-MOH-ee").
question.answerHtml: Mau [accept Mau Movement; accept Mau a Pule; accept O le Mau; reject “Mau Mau”]

swap.leadin: Identify the following relating to the problem of longitude, FTPE.
swap.text: The K-1 clock made by Larcum Kendall, based on the design of Harrison, served as an aide for this British captain who was killed by Hawaiians in February of 1779.
swap.clue: This figure, although not trained as a scientist, nevertheless received the Royal Society's Copley Medal for techniques that he developed to prevent his crew from contracting scurvy on lengthy Pacific voyages.

question.text: The Counter Revolutionary Warfare Unit was the brainchild of this officer, who orchestrated both Fijian coups of 1987. This man, nicknamed "Rambo," then served as prime minister from 1992 until his 1999 loss to Mahendra Chaudry.

swap.text: During the Vietnam War, Holt and this Prime Minister of New Zealand aided the US war effort per the terms of the ANZUS pact. Nicknamed "Kiwi Keith," this leader of the National Party remains the only New Zealand politician to have served as both prime minister and governor-general.
swap.clue: This man who appointed Robert Muldoon as his Minister of Finance and faced harsh criticism for sending military support to the Vietnam War.
